observations: Photo 0 shows the front of a smartphone with a purple/pink gradient lock screen, time 05:03, date Saturday, March 22, and a notch at the top. The screen has visible smudges and fingerprints. The phone is held in a hand with a patterned shirt cuff visible.

Photo 1 shows the back of the same phone, which is purple with a triple-camera module in the top left corner and an Apple logo in the center. The phone appears to be an iPhone 14 Pro Max based on the camera design and size.
In the background of both photos, a white box with 'iPhone' visible is on a shelf, suggesting the phone may be in a retail or resale environment.
Watermarks 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'CEE-GADGETS LTD' are overlaid on both photos.
No serial number, model number, or IMEI is visible in either photo.

claims.evidence: Photo 1 shows the triple-camera module and design consistent with iPhone 14 Pro Max. The seller's claim of '14 Promax' is supported by visual evidence.
No SIM tray, settings screen, or network status is visible. The lock status cannot be confirmed from photos alone.
Storage capacity is not visible on the screen or in any photo. Cannot be confirmed remotely.

risks.risk: Phone may be network-locked or have restrictions preventing use on other carriers.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the Settings > General > About section showing the carrier lock status, or a video of the phone attempting to insert a SIM card.
risks.if_unproven: priced as network-locked, which reduces value significantly in Lagos market

risks.risk: Storage capacity may not be 128GB as claimed.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the Settings > General > About section showing the actual storage capacity.
risks.if_unproven: priced as lower storage (e.g., 64GB), which reduces value

risks.risk: Phone may have screen damage, dead pixels, or software issues not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video of the phone being used, showing full screen functionality, camera operation, and responsiveness.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially faulty or with hidden defects

risks.risk: Phone may be stolen or have an iCloud lock (blacklisted).
risks.proof: A screenshot of the Settings > [User] > iCloud > Find My iPhone showing 'Find My iPhone' turned off, or a video of the phone being erased and set up as new.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially blacklisted, which reduces value or makes it unsellable

proof_requests: Screenshot of Settings > General > About showing model, storage, and carrier lock status.
Video of the phone being turned on, showing full screen functionality and camera operation.
Screenshot or video showing the phone being erased and set up as new to confirm no iCloud lock.
Photo of the SIM tray or a video showing SIM insertion and network activation.
response.reason: While the phone is visually identifiable as an iPhone 14 Pro Max, critical claims about network lock status, storage capacity, and iCloud lock cannot be verified from the photos alone. These factors significantly affect price and usability in the Lagos market. Proof is required to determine the true condition and value.
